key_insight: The paper argues that agents should stop re-deciding the same control logic in every task and instead grow that logic into reusable code. This lets the LLM focus on semantic reasoning while the harness handles repeated execution strategy.
problem_solved: It addresses the inefficiency of LLM agents that repeatedly reconstruct the same control decisions inside each task context, which wastes context, compute, and reliability across streams of related tasks.
method: Start from a strategy-free scaffold that exposes failure points instead of hard-coded policies.
Use task feedback to learn recurring control behavior as executable harness code.
Reserve LLM calls for task-specific reasoning, while reusable harness components handle repeated orchestration decisions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a way to build more efficient, scalable agents that reuse learned control strategies across tasks. It can reduce context bloat, improve consistency, and lower the cost of agent deployment over long task streams.

paper_title: Grow the Harness, Not the Context: From Strategy-Free Scaffolds to Reusable Specialist Agents
paper_authors: Laizhen Li, Jiarui Li, Juanjuan Zhao, Kejiang Ye, Ye Li
